summary: APAC region pin set but some requests served from US during capacity spikes — confirm data residency and mitigation options
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (KumoHealth) has configured region pinning to ap-southeast-1 for all hosted API calls. During a capacity spike on 2026-03-10 they observed increased tail latency and traces that show compute nodes in us-east-1 serving several requests. Customer is asking: did their request payloads leave APAC? What parts of request/metadata cross regions? What are supported mitigations (strict residency, fail-if-cross-region, dedicated capacity)?

Impact:
- Enterprise customer in regulated healthcare use case concerned about data sovereignty and audit controls.
- Observed latency spike impacting UI flows (patients and clinicians).

Environment:
- Hosted API (redwood public), prod - ap-southeast-1 region pin set via customer config.
- Customer account ID: KUMO-001 (internal ref).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send generation request with region=ap-southeast-1 pinned via SDK header X-Redwood-Region: ap-southeast-1.
2) Repeat during peak load window (2026-03-10 17:30-18:15 SGT).
3) Observe response latency increase and service trace indicating serving_region: us-east-1 for subset of requests.

Observed behavior:
- ~8% of requests in the window were served by us-east-1 compute.
- Token-level latency for those requests increased ~2.6s compared to fully ap-southeast-1 flows.
- Customer concerned that PII may have crossed regions.

Expected behavior:
- With region pin set, customer expects all inference compute to remain in ap-southeast-1 or a clear failure when capacity unavailable.

Attachments and IDs:
- Sample request IDs: req_20260310_1a2b3c, req_20260310_1a2b3d, req_20260310_1a2b3f
- Trace links (internal): https://observability.prod/redwood/traces/req_20260310_1a2b3c
- Screenshot of SDK header config attached in ticket.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:05 - KumoHealth (Sara Lim): We saw ~8% of requests served from us-east-1; need confirmation that customer data did not leave APAC. This is blocking compliance signoff.
2026-03-10 11:27 - Maya Chen (Customer Support): Thanks Sara — escalating to SRE and network. Sharing sample request IDs. Will follow up with timeline and mitigation options.

2026-03-11 08:12 - Jordan Patel (SRE): Started triage, pulling routing and trace logs for provided request IDs. Noted some routing decisions for those trace IDs show fallback. Investigating which policy triggered fallback.

2026-03-12 14:40 - Jordan Patel (SRE): Preliminary finding: control-plane routing selected a compatible model pool in us-east-1 for a short window when ap-southeast-1 free capacity < threshold. Collecting packet-level and audit-log evidence for data flow path.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Product (Lina Gomez): Flagging this to product for visibility — we should clarify residency semantics in docs and consider a customer-visible strict_residency option.

2026-03-13 09:30 - Maya Chen (Customer Support): KumoHealth requested an immediate mitigation: prefer failing requests over cross-region fallback. Asked for timeline to implement mitigation or apply a routing override.
2026-03-13 11:00 - Jordan Patel (SRE): Applied temporary routing override for KUMO-001 to enforce fail-on-cross-region for next 48 hours. Monitoring for errors and customer impact.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 - pulled router decision logs for req_20260310_1a2b3c and req_20260310_1a2b3d. Decision path: API gateway -> control-plane policy evaluation -> model-pool lookup -> assign compute node (us-east-1).

Capacity snapshot 2026-03-10 17:35 SGT shows ap-southeast-1 free slots at 12% below the configured soft-threshold for automatic fallback prevention. During this brief window, routing policy allowed cross-region fallback to preserve availability (configurable per-customer default: allow_fallback=true).

Audit log review: request metadata (headers, request_id, trace_id) were propagated to control-plane components in our global control plane. Payload bodies are encrypted in transit. No evidence of logging of plaintext customer payloads in control-plane logs. Compute nodes in us-east-1 received the encrypted payload and performed inference there.

Network traces (tcpdump) from compute nodes show connections served entirely within provider backbone; because compute was in us-east-1, egress did not flow back to ap-southeast-1 compute. Therefore compute did process the request in us-east-1 for the affected traces.
Customer uses healthcare PII workload — this is a policy violation for their residency requirements when compute crosses regions.
logs: [2026-03-10T17:34:12Z] routing: req=req_20260310_1a2b3c policy=region_pin(ap-southeast-1) allow_fallback=true chosen_region=us-east-1 reason=capacity_shortfall
[2026-03-10T17:34:13Z] compute(us-east-1): started inference req=req_20260310_1a2b3c model=rw-instruct-large-v1 latency=2800ms
resolution:
Temporary mitigation applied: SRE applied a routing override for customer KUMO-001 to fail requests (429) if capacity in ap-southeast-1 is insufficient for the next 48 hours. Customer notified and verified that subsequent requests either served from ap-southeast-1 or failed with a clear 429 and message 'region capacity unavailable - strict residency enforced'.

Longer-term outcome: recommended Dedicated reserved capacity or Private deployment for strict data residency SLAs. Product has been asked to prioritize exposing a customer-facing 'strict_residency' toggle and documentation clarifying what 'region pin' guarantees for hosted plans.

Ticket remains in-progress until product accepts PR and we confirm the routing override behavior in the console.
